Hey. Haven't posted much in awhile because I don't have much to say all the time, but you might remember me as the guy who works at Chipotle.

I have been going at it for awhile now and I'm about to leave the (fantastic)company because I'm moving, and there's no branches near Bremerton. So, I have decided to share some of my final thoughts from the store.

There has no be more of us

I can't honestly imagine that there aren't more secret shitlords who are friends with obeasts just because they want to fit in. I see co-workers come in, one skinny, one obeast, talking about dieting and losing weight or being healthy. Maybe skipping the beans or only getting a regular portion of cheese instead of extra. The humans see their friends skip the meat to opt for a veggie bowl, thinking it's a healthier choice, only to take advantage of the free guac. Guac has 100 more calories than our chicken per 4 oz. How do the humans put up with this? How do they not want to say anything? We serve a few clinics and hospitals on the reg and the amount of unhealthy health practitioners is vomit inducing. And the fact that if you confront anyone about it, they just say HAES. God. Damn.

Things fats do when dieting at Chipotle

  1. They eat at Chipotle. They're pretty much already losing at dieting. It's possible, but unlikely

  2. "I'll just get chips and guac today". Not realizing that the guac is 260 calories and a bag of chips is just over 500. That's about a bowls worth of calories without any of the nutrition.

  3. Veggie bowls for weight loss. Veggie bowls come with free guac. And they use that either on the side for a bag of chips(even the small bags add 130 calories) or they get it on the bowl adding more calories than the eat would in the first place.

  4. They think that brown rice is healthy, so they get more of this and less of other things. I honestly don't get this one. I can't justify their thought. Is it better than white1? Sure. But that doesn't mean it's good for you.

  5. Our 2oz portion of vinaigrette has 220 calories. So they eschew rice, get a salad and ask for a vinaigrette. Look who's back at the exact same amount of calories.

Other shit they do

  • 3 fucking vinaigrettes. It's oil and honey. 2oz is 220 calories. And you're getting 3.

  • The 'family man' regular who comes in and gets 2 bowls to go. Sure, he could have a SO who doesn't ever want to come with him, but maybe you're going home and devouring both for yourself, like that one time you did it in the store and felt so ashamed you started getting it to go. Yeah. I fucking know you. You're lucky I get paid more than minimum wage to provide excellent service or jesus christ I would rip you a new one.

*Side quesadillas. 2 small quesadillas on the side with sour cream for each. Like fucking really. That's literally another meal. Another 600 calories. Or the guys who get a large one with a side or two of sour. Another 600 to 800 calories there. I just can't fucking stand being forced to aid their poor choices.

1Last time I was here people got into a spat about brown v white rice. Brown in healthier at Chipotle because we use less salt and oil in it.

I always see fatties at Chipotle and Baja Fresh. Chipotle doesn't even look healthy. The whole menu looks like calorie overload. I don't understand how people could think that it is. Baja Fresh on the other hand, has that healthy vibe, all white, clean, and basically the exact same 1000 calorie food. I go there every other month with people I work with and the fatasses talk about how it's nice to eat healthy every once and awhile. I mentioned to one guy that with the chips, guac, soda and burrito he was well over 1000 calories, and he said, "Oh, well... at least it looks healthy, and no MSG."
It's 2015, anyone still afraid of msg needs to be curb stomped.

The only time I have eaten at Chipotle was when I went to a hockey game. I was starving but I don't really like burritos so I got a plain cheese quesadilla. OMG, sooooooo greasy. Way too much cheese. However I hadn't had lunch so I guess it was okay.

I explicitly go to Chipotle to bulk - how anyone goes there expecting to lose weight is beyond me. There are less caloric options, but it's kind of like the old "I'll have a triple cheeseburger, large chili fries, and a DIET coke (cutting calories, teehee!)"
Counting the calories consumed by the customers who come into my workplace is my favorite thing to do. It keeps me cheerful on long shifts.

I'm probably the only one that thinks this way, but anything less than 800 calories isn't a meal, that's a snack.

I can't even recall the last day I burned under 3000 calories.
